reason: Drift verified in b.css and on the page: "Saturday 3 October 2026" is .b-when 30/1.3 on owner, desk, print and 20/1.3 on phone, but .b-dayDate 20/1.4 on day; moment titles run .b-title 24/1.3 against .b-dayNowTitle 24/1.2; .b-stepRead is 15px mono at --lead-body 1.5. sharpenedFix: Bind leading to role token, not per class: .b-when and .b-dayDate both take --lead-date; .b-title and .b-dayNowTitle both take --lead-head, which already declares 24/30/38 (today .b-title wrongly borrows --lead-date); .b-stepRead takes --lead-label, declared for mono. Then fix the gate at its real seam rather than adding a check that exists: leadingRole is scoped per state and keys on size, so the same date string at 20px passes at 1.3 and 1.4. Accumulate its map across all eleven states and key it on a declared role marker (data-type on the element), not on rendered size.
